bills.title: 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Commemorative Coin Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate.
bills.nexus: H.R. 1993 authorizes the U.S. Mint, a Treasury bureau, to design, produce, and sell commemorative coins marking the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001. Treasury's implementation interest centers on Mint production capacity, surcharge revenue flow to designated beneficiaries, and ensuring the program complies with the statutory commemorative coin limits Congress sets each year.

bills.title: No Tax Dollars for Terrorists Act
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 330.
bills.nexus: H.R. 260 would restrict the use of federal funds from reaching designated terrorist organizations, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and its sanctions enforcement authorities. Treasury must assess whether the bill duplicates, conflicts with, or creates new compliance obligations beyond existing OFAC sanctions programs and any interagency fund-monitoring mechanisms.

bills.title: Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act
bills.status: Became Public Law No: 119-36.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2808 amends the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act's financial privacy provisions, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Consumer Policy and the Financial Stability Oversight Council's oversight of data-sharing practices among financial institutions. The implementation risk centers on ensuring mortgage lenders and affiliated data brokers update consumer notice and opt-out procedures in compliance with the new restrictions, with potential examination and enforcement coordination required across banking regulators.

bills.title: Enhancing Multi-Class Share Disclosures Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3357 touches the Securities and Exchange Commission's disclosure framework for multi-class share structures, an area where Treasury's Office of Domestic Finance monitors capital markets integrity and investor protection policy. The implementation risk centers on whether enhanced disclosure requirements could affect IPO market activity and the cost of capital formation, both of which have downstream implications for Treasury's broader financial markets oversight responsibilities.

bills.title: Financial Technology Protection Act of 2025
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2384 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence (TFI) and FinCEN by directing the establishment of a working group to combat terrorist and illicit use of digital assets. Treasury bears implementation risk because it would likely lead or co-lead interagency coordination efforts and could require new regulatory guidance or rulemaking on digital asset oversight within existing BSA/AML frameworks.

bills.title: Equal Opportunity for All Investors Act of 2025
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3339 touches the SEC's accredited investor definition under the Securities Act of 1933, which intersects with Treasury's interest in capital formation policy and financial stability oversight through FSOC. Treasury should monitor implementation risk around expanded retail access to private markets, including potential systemic exposure if less sophisticated investors concentrate in illiquid or high-risk securities.

bills.title: Greenlighting Growth Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3343 lacks a documented nexus to Treasury in the available record, so the specific office or authority implicated cannot be confirmed at this time. Legislative Affairs should query the bill's full text to determine whether provisions touch OFR, OCC, FinCEN, or another Treasury component before assessing implementation or fiscal risk.

bills.title: Improving Access to Small Business Information Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3351 touches the Small Business Administration's information-sharing framework, which intersects with Treasury's Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization and any interagency coordination requirements under existing SBA-Treasury lending and contracting programs. Treasury's implementation risk lies in potential new data-sharing or reporting obligations that could affect how Treasury offices access or transmit small business eligibility information across federal systems.

bills.title: Middle Market IPO Cost Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3395 would reduce SEC registration and reporting cost burdens for middle-market companies pursuing IPOs, directly touching the Office of Domestic Finance's capital markets policy portfolio and Treasury's interest in efficient, well-functioning public equity markets. The implementation risk centers on whether scaled disclosure standards adequately balance investor protection against fraud with the goal of broadening public market access for smaller issuers.

bills.title: Small Entity Update Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3382 likely touches the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and its beneficial ownership reporting framework under the Corporate Transparency Act, which falls under Treasury's anti-money laundering authorities. Treasury's implementation risk centers on potential changes to small-entity exemption thresholds or reporting deadlines that could disrupt FinCEN's ongoing CTA rollout and compliance infrastructure.

bills.title: Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act
bills.status: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
bills.nexus: H.R. 1919 directly targets the Federal Reserve and Treasury's authority under the Federal Reserve Act by prohibiting the issuance of a retail central bank digital currency, placing constraints on any future digital dollar initiative. Treasury's implementation risk centers on the potential limitation of financial infrastructure modernization options and the precedent it sets for congressional restriction of monetary tool development.

bills.title: An act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14.
bills.status: Became Public Law No: 119-21.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because this reconciliation law directly affects tax revenue and spending provisions under the jurisdiction of the Internal Revenue Service and the Office of Tax Policy. The implementation risk centers on IRS capacity to administer any new or modified tax provisions on compressed timelines while maintaining compliance and revenue collection integrity.

bills.title: Access to Small Business Investor Capital Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2225 amends the Small Business Investment Act to ease restrictions on SBIC fund structures, touching Treasury's interest through its role in federal credit and budget scoring of Small Business Administration debenture guarantees that carry Treasury backstop exposure. Treasury's Office of Legislative Affairs and the Office of Fiscal Affairs should track implementation risk around any expanded leverage ratios or licensing changes that could increase contingent federal liability.

bills.title: ELEVATE Act of 2025
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus:
The ELEVATE Act of 2025 likely touches Treasury's Office of Domestic Finance and potentially CDFI Fund or FinCEN authorities, depending on its provisions related to financial access or lending structures. Treasury would monitor implementation risk around any regulatory mandates, capital requirements, or reporting obligations that fall within its supervisory or programmatic jurisdiction.

*(Note: Without the bill text or a confirmed nexus on file, this assessment is based on the title and referral to Senate Banking; recommend pulling the enrolled text to confirm specific Treasury equities before briefing.)*

bills.title: HALOS Act of 2025
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: The HALOS Act of 2025 amends the securities laws governing "test-the-waters" and demo day communications, directly implicating Treasury's interest in capital formation policy and its coordination role with the SEC on securities regulation affecting small businesses and startups. Treasury should monitor implementation risk around any exemptions from Securities Act registration requirements, as poorly scoped safe harbors could be exploited for fraudulent offerings or undermine investor protection frameworks Treasury supports through its broader financial stability mandate.

bills.title: Fair Investment Opportunities for Professional Experts Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3394 would expand the SEC's "accredited investor" definition to include individuals with professional credentials or expertise, touching the SEC's investor-qualification framework that Treasury monitors through its role in capital markets policy and the Financial Stability Oversight Council. Treasury's implementation concern is that broadening retail access to private, often illiquid offerings increases the risk of investor harm and potential systemic stress if losses in private markets become widespread among newly qualified participants.

bills.title: Encouraging Public Offerings Act of 2025
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3381 amends Securities Act and Exchange Act provisions governing the IPO on-ramp and testing-the-waters communications, touching Treasury's Office of Capital Markets and its oversight interest in equity market structure and investor protection frameworks. Implementation risk centers on whether expanded emerging-growth-company eligibility and extended confidential filing windows could reduce disclosure quality, creating downstream systemic exposure Treasury would need to monitor through its Financial Stability Oversight Council role.

bills.title: American Entrepreneurs First Act of 2025
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2966 likely touches Treasury's Office of Small Business Programs and potentially IRS or SBA-coordinated tax incentive authorities depending on its financing or credit provisions. Treasury should monitor implementation risk around any tax-preferred capital access mechanisms or federal lending guarantees that could affect revenue estimates or financial regulatory compliance burdens.

bills.title: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
bills.status: Became Public Law No: 119-4.
bills.nexus: H.R. 1968 directly affects Treasury's Office of Management and Budget-apportioned funding levels and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service's appropriations authority by extending full-year spending at prior-year rates, constraining discretionary program operations across departmental offices. The implementation risk centers on Treasury's inability to initiate new programs or realign resources mid-year, creating execution constraints for IRS modernization, financial intelligence operations under FinCEN, and debt management activities under the Office of Domestic Finance.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide special rules for the taxation of certain residents of Taiwan with income from sources within the United States.
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: H.R. 33 directly implicates IRS and the Office of Tax Policy, as it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to create a preferential tax regime for Taiwanese residents earning U.S.-sourced income, a function currently governed by standard withholding and residency rules in the absence of a formal U.S.-Taiwan tax treaty. Treasury faces implementation risk in designing administrable special rules outside the treaty framework, as well as revenue scoring obligations and potential precedent concerns if similar carve-outs are sought for other non-treaty jurisdictions.
